narrativeReportMd:
# PractitionerRole R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`PractitionerRole` keeps the same canonical identity, but it has two hard local instance-shape breaks: R4 `telecom` is replaced by R6 `contact`, and the R4 availability fields are replaced by a single R6 `availability` datatype element. R6 also adds optional directory metadata that is not cleanly representable in R4.

## Scope
The report covers local `PractitionerRole` element, type, binding, flag, and semantic changes in the core StructureDefinitions. Inherited base-resource changes are excluded and listed as out of scope.

## Main migration themes
The main migration work is not new required data; no retained local element became mandatory. The risk is wire-shape and code-generation churn: contact details and availability schedules moved to different element names and richer datatypes, so strict validators and generated R4 classes will reject the old/new shapes without transforms.

## Highest-impact findings
The highest-impact findings are `PractitionerRole.telecom` removal/replacement and the availability model replacement. Both can make otherwise valid R4 instances invalid under R6 validation until transformed.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is most useful for contact and availability migration policy: deciding how to preserve new R6 contact subfields in R4-compatible stores, how to map free-text availability exceptions, and how to handle R4 all-day availability records that also carried start/end times.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Most hard breaks could have been softened by temporarily retaining deprecated R4 elements or publishing explicit cross-version extensions. The R6 model is more expressive and reusable, but it requires deliberate transforms.

## Follow-up analysis
Separate analysis should cover the new `Availability` and `ExtendedContactDetail` datatypes, PractitionerRole search parameter changes, and inherited `Resource`/`DomainResource` changes.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `PractitionerRole` has hard local breaking changes in contact and availability serialization. Top migration concerns are transforming `telecom` to `contact.telecom`, transforming old schedule fields into `availability`, and preserving R6-only directory data when round-tripping to R4. Confidence is high for element-shape changes and lower for terminology-expansion details.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Migration is mostly structural. Existing R4 instances with `telecom`, `availableTime`, `notAvailable`, or `availabilityExceptions` need explicit field-name and datatype transforms before R6 validation. R6-to-R4 conversion is lossy for richer `ExtendedContactDetail`, `Availability.period`, optional description-less `notAvailableTime`, and new directory metadata such as `network`, `display`, `characteristic`, and `communication` unless extensions are used.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for local StructureDefinition element presence, cardinality, type, reference target, binding-strength, modifier, and summary flag comparisons because both core JSON StructureDefinitions were available. Confidence is medium for terminology content and rationale because no official diff/change note or terminology-server expansion was available.

findings.title: PractitionerRole.telecom was removed and replaced by PractitionerRole.contact

oldState.summary: R4 had a local 0..* `telecom` element of type ContactPoint and marked it as a summary element.

semanticText.short: Contact details that are specific to the role/location/service
semanticText.definition: Contact details that are specific to the role/location/service.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 stored role-specific phone, fax, email, or URL details directly in `PractitionerRole.telecom` as repeated `ContactPoint` values.

newState.summary: R6 removes `telecom` and adds 0..* `contact` of type ExtendedContactDetail. The resource-level `contact` element is not a summary element, while the nested datatype has summary subfields including `telecom`.

semanticText.short: Official contact details relating to this PractitionerRole
semanticText.definition: The contact details of communication devices available relevant to the specific PractitionerRole. This can include addresses, phone numbers, fax numbers, mobile numbers, email addresses and web sites.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses `PractitionerRole.contact`, whose `ExtendedContactDetail` datatype can carry `purpose`, `name`, `telecom`, `address`, `organization`, and `period`.

facts.note: The nested ExtendedContactDetail fields are summary=true, but PractitionerRole.contact itself is summary=false in the inspected StructureDefinition.
The ContactPoint content moves under the ExtendedContactDetail datatype.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R4 element definition and requirements for role/location/service contact details correspond directly to the R6 `contact` definition and the `ExtendedContactDetail.telecom` subelement. The match is a representation replacement, not a simple rename, because the R6 datatype adds purpose, name, address, organization, and period.

impact.impactRationaleMd: A strict R6 validator will reject an R4 instance that still contains `PractitionerRole.telecom` because that local element no longer exists. Generated model code also changes from a repeated `ContactPoint` property to a repeated `ExtendedContactDetail` property. In the reverse direction, R6 contact records can contain address, purpose, named person, handling organization, and contact period that do not fit in R4 `telecom` without loss or extensions.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Directory contact details are operationally important for scheduling, referrals, and patient/provider communication. Loss or misplacement of contact data can disrupt care coordination even if it is not usually a clinical decision-support safety field.

justification.inferredGoal: Use a richer, reusable contact datatype that can represent contact purpose, responsible person or organization, address, telecom details, and validity period.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated PractitionerRole.telecom while adding PractitionerRole.contact; this would preserve old ContactPoint instances but only as a transitional/duplicate base representation.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of a richer reusable contact model is reasonable, and the break is probably justified because the less-breaking base design would create a lasting duplicate representation for the same contact endpoints. The old shape can be mapped mechanically for common cases, but retaining it in base R6 would complicate validation, search, summaries, and authoring rules.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Best less-breaking base design: keep R4 `PractitionerRole.telecom` as a deprecated `0..* ContactPoint` element while adding `PractitionerRole.contact` / `ExtendedContactDetail`, with guidance or invariants to avoid using both for the same endpoint. This would preserve most R4-valid instances, but it is only a partial alternative because R6 would have two same-resource places for role contact endpoints and no perfect way to prevent divergence.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Material duplicate contact semantics: telecom and contact.telecom could diverge, validators and search must reconcile both, and deprecated same-resource fields may persist indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 defines `PractitionerRole.telecom` with cardinality 0..*, type ContactPoint, and isSummary true.
evidence.quote: Contact details that are specific to the role/location/service.

evidence.detail: R6 defines `PractitionerRole.contact` with cardinality 0..*, type ExtendedContactDetail, and isSummary false; no local `PractitionerRole.telecom` element exists.
evidence.quote: Official contact details relating to this PractitionerRole

evidence.detail: The R6 datatype contains nested 0..* `telecom` ContactPoint values plus purpose, name, address, organization, and period.

examples.examplesMd: The examples are minimal fragments. The first shows an R4 field name that becomes invalid in R6. The second shows R6 contact details that cannot be represented by R4 `telecom` alone.

findings.narrativeMd: `PractitionerRole.telecom` is not present in R6. Its replacement, `PractitionerRole.contact`, is not a direct `ContactPoint` list but a richer `ExtendedContactDetail` list. This is a hard validation and code-generation break for systems that deserialize, validate, search, or render role contact details through the old property name.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances containing `telecom` can be valid in R4 but invalid against the R6 resource definition until transformed. A straightforward R4-to-R6 transform can wrap each old `ContactPoint` in an `ExtendedContactDetail.telecom` entry. The transform is not fully reversible once R6 uses contact purpose, name, address, organization, or period. Systems that rely on `_summary`-style behavior should also check behavior because R4 `telecom` was summary=true while R6 `PractitionerRole.contact` is summary=false.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Map each R4 `PractitionerRole.telecom[n]` to an R6 `PractitionerRole.contact[n].telecom[0]` or group multiple telecom points into one contact only when local policy says they share the same purpose/person/period. For R6-to-R4, preserve `contact.purpose`, `name`, `address`, `organization`, and `period` in extensions or sidecar data if round-trip fidelity is required. Test direct validation, generated model serialization, summary responses, and UI rendering of contact details.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A backward-compatible design could have retained `telecom` as deprecated while adding `contact`. That would have avoided immediate instance rejection but created duplicate contact channels. The R6 design is cleaner and more expressive but makes a migration transform mandatory for existing R4 data.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Review local policy for whether multiple R4 telecom repetitions should become separate R6 contacts or one contact with multiple `telecom` entries.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 `PractitionerRole.telecom` was a repeatable `ContactPoint`; R6 removes that wire element and uses repeatable `PractitionerRole.contact` of `ExtendedContactDetail`, with the old contact points nested under `contact.telecom`. A directory server or generated client that sends or reads `telecom` must transform data or change property access, so this is a real path-level break. The forward transform is usually mechanical, and the R6 datatype adds purpose, named contact, address, organization, and period rather than merely renaming a field. Preserving `telecom` in base R6 would reduce migration friction but would also leave competing contact representations in the same resource, so the break looks proportionate.
keyEvidence: R6 StructureDefinition-PractitionerRole: no local `PractitionerRole.telecom`; `PractitionerRole.contact` is 0..* `ExtendedContactDetail`, summary=false.
R6 StructureDefinition-ExtendedContactDetail: nested `ExtendedContactDetail.telecom` is 0..* `ContactPoint` and the datatype also has purpose, name, address, organization, and period.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 PractitionerRole is FMM 2 and trial-use, which is neutral: it does not erase the wire/API break, but it also does not create normative stability pressure. The coherent R6 datatype goal and feasible migration path dominate the judgment.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen: untransformed R4 instances containing `telecom` are not valid against the R6 resource shape, and generated models change from a direct `ContactPoint[]` property to `ExtendedContactDetail[]`; R6-to-R4 conversion can also lose richer contact fields.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: A less-breaking base design could have kept deprecated `telecom` while adding `contact`, possibly with guidance or an invariant discouraging both. That would preserve old instances but creates duplicate contact channels, conflict/precedence rules, summary-behavior questions, and long-lived support for the obsolete representation.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing high hard-break and runtime assessment. I do not treat a less-breaking alternative as wholly unavailable, but the plausible alternative has enough duplicate-representation cost that it does not change the final judgment.

findings.title: R4 availability fields were replaced by R6 PractitionerRole.availability

oldState.summary: R4 had local scheduling elements: `availableTime` 0..*, `notAvailable` 0..*, and `availabilityExceptions` 0..1.

semanticText.definition: R4 represented availability through two local BackboneElements and a free-text availability-exceptions string. `notAvailable.description` was required when `notAvailable` was present.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 represented availability directly on `PractitionerRole`, with `availableTime.daysOfWeek`, `allDay`, start/end time, `notAvailable.description`, `notAvailable.during`, and `availabilityExceptions`.

newState.summary: R6 replaces the local scheduling fields with one optional `availability` element of type Availability.

constraints.expression: allDay.exists().not() or (allDay implies availableStartTime.exists().not() and availableEndTime.exists().not())
constraints.human: Cannot include start/end times when selecting all day availability.

semanticText.short: Times the Practitioner is available at this location and/or healthcare service (including exceptions)
semanticText.definition: A collection of times the practitioner is available or performing this role at the location and/or healthcareservice.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 uses the reusable `Availability` datatype, where `availableTime` and `notAvailableTime` are nested inside `PractitionerRole.availability`; it also adds an optional `Availability.period`.

facts.newValue: No exact top-level field; can be approximated by Availability.notAvailableTime.description

facts.note: R6 Availability.notAvailableTime.description is optional, which creates reverse-conversion risk to R4.
R6 forbids start/end times when allDay is true; R4 only said such times were ignored.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The R6 `Availability` datatype has nested `availableTime` and `notAvailableTime` components with names and meanings matching the R4 local BackboneElements, so this is a high-confidence structural replacement. `availabilityExceptions` is less exact because R6 represents textual exceptions through `notAvailableTime.description` rather than a separate top-level string.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An R4 instance containing `availableTime`, `notAvailable`, or `availabilityExceptions` uses element names that are absent from the R6 `PractitionerRole` definition. R6 generated code also replaces two local BackboneElement collections and a string with a single `Availability` datatype property. Reverse conversion is possible for common cases but is lossy or profile-dependent for `Availability.period`, optional description-less not-available periods, and free-text exception semantics.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Availability is operationally important for directories and scheduling. Incorrect conversion can show a practitioner as available or unavailable at the wrong times.

justification.inferredGoal: Reuse a common Availability datatype and support richer availability context consistently across resources.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated availableTime, notAvailable, and availabilityExceptions while adding PractitionerRole.availability; optionally introduce the allDay/start-end rule as warning-first.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of using a common `Availability` datatype and adding clearer scheduling semantics is reasonable. A less-breaking design could preserve R4 field names, but it would burden base R6 with parallel ways to say the same availability facts, including conflict handling between old fields and `availability`. Given those material interoperability and validation costs, the breaking replacement is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Best less-breaking base design: keep the R4 local availability fields as deprecated aliases while adding `PractitionerRole.availability`, and make the new all-day/start-end constraint transitional guidance or a warning before enforcing it. This would preserve many R4-valid instances, including old field names, but only partially meets the R6 goal because the base resource would carry two availability models that implementations must reconcile.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Material duplicate scheduling semantics: old local fields and the Availability datatype could conflict, require reconciliation rules, and leave redundant schedule representations in the base resource indefinitely.

evidence.detail: R4 defines local availability fields directly under PractitionerRole, including repeated available and not-available BackboneElements and a string exception field.
R6 defines a single 0..1 local `availability` element of type Availability and does not define the old local fields.
evidence.quote: Times the Practitioner is available at this location and/or healthcare service (including exceptions)

evidence.detail: The R6 Availability datatype contains nested repeated available/not-available components and adds the av-1 error invariant for all-day availability.

examples.examplesMd: The R4 example is valid by local R4 element names; after a naive transform it would also need policy for the R6 `av-1` invariant because R4 said start/end times were ignored when `allDay=true`, while R6 forbids them.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 removes the R4 local availability schedule fields and introduces `PractitionerRole.availability`. This is a shape change, not just a semantic clarification. Implementations with generated R4 models, JSON serializers, FHIRPath expressions, or UI bindings for `availableTime`, `notAvailable`, or `availabilityExceptions` must change to the `Availability` datatype shape.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Untransformed R4 instances using the old field names are invalid in R6. A structured transform can preserve most `availableTime` and `notAvailable` repetitions by nesting them under `availability`. However, R6 adds a computable error constraint forbidding start/end times when `allDay` is true; R4 only documented those times as ignored. R6-to-R4 conversion is not always clean because R6 `Availability.period` has no R4 equivalent and R6 `notAvailableTime.description` can be absent even though R4 `notAvailable.description` was mandatory.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create an explicit availability transform. Map R4 `availableTime[]` to R6 `availability.availableTime[]`, `notAvailable[]` to `availability.notAvailableTime[]`, and consider mapping `availabilityExceptions` to a `notAvailableTime.description` entry when no more precise period is available. Drop or review start/end times when `allDay=true` before R6 validation. For R6-to-R4, use extensions or manual review for `Availability.period` and not-available periods with no description.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The reusable datatype likely improves consistency across resources, but the same goal could have been introduced less disruptively by retaining deprecated old fields during a transition period. The stricter `av-1` invariant is also a behavior change for old all-day records with times; a warning-first approach would have been less disruptive but less precise.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Pay special attention to local data where `allDay=true` coexists with start/end times and to text-only `availabilityExceptions` that do not identify a period.

freshReview.narrativeMd: R4 exposed scheduling fields directly on PractitionerRole: `availableTime`, `notAvailable`, and `availabilityExceptions`. R6 replaces them with one optional `availability` element of datatype `Availability`, whose children carry the available and unavailable periods. Untransformed R4 instances and generated-code references to the old names break, and availability data can affect scheduling. However, most forward migration is a structural nesting transform, and the reusable datatype is a reasonable R6 modeling goal. Keeping both old local fields and the new datatype would create competing schedule sources and precedence problems.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition-PractitionerRole: `availableTime` and `notAvailable` are 0..* BackboneElements; `availabilityExceptions` is 0..1 string.
R6 StructureDefinition-PractitionerRole: `PractitionerRole.availability` is 0..1 `Availability`; the old local fields are absent.
R6 StructureDefinition-Availability: `availableTime` and `notAvailableTime` are repeatable nested elements, and `av-1` is an error invariant forbidding start/end times when `allDay` is true.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 PractitionerRole is FMM 2 and trial-use, so maturity is a neutral factor. The operational importance of scheduling matters, but the resource did not have a mature or normative stability expectation in R4.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: old-valid/new-invalid plus runtime/API/codegen: R4 instances using the removed local scheduling fields fail the R6 wire shape until transformed, and generated APIs move from local BackboneElement collections plus a string to an `Availability` datatype. There is also limited R6-to-R4 loss for R6-only availability details and optional description-less unavailable periods.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: R6 could have retained the old fields as deprecated aliases while adding `availability`, or could have introduced the `av-1` rule first as a warning. Those choices would preserve more old data but would duplicate schedule semantics, require conflict rules when old and new fields disagree, and weaken the reusable-datatype cleanup.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree with the existing hard-break/high-impact assessment for untransformed data. I see plausible less-breaking transitional designs, but their duplicate-schedule cost makes the current R6 design probably acceptable.

findings.title: R6 adds optional directory metadata not representable in R4 PractitionerRole

oldState.summary: R4 has no local equivalents for network, display, characteristic, or communication on PractitionerRole.
oldState.narrativeMd: In R4, implementers generally had to infer these concepts from referenced resources, use extensions, or omit them.

newState.summary: R6 adds `network` 0..* Reference(Organization), `display` 0..1 string, `characteristic` 0..* CodeableConcept, and `communication` 0..* CodeableConcept with a required all-languages binding.
newState.narrativeMd: These additions make R6 PractitionerRole richer for directories and patient-facing search, but they create new data that an R4 base instance cannot carry without extensions.

facts.note: 0..* CodeableConcept, required binding to all-languages with starter languages additional binding.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: These are local R6 elements with no same-name or clearly equivalent local R4 elements in the R4 PractitionerRole StructureDefinition.

impact.impactRationaleMd: The additions do not make old R4 instances invalid in R6 because all are optional. They do matter for down-conversion and mixed-version systems: an R6 instance using these fields is not a valid base R4 PractitionerRole and cannot be represented without extensions, lossy dropping, or mapping to other resources/profile-specific fields.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Networks, display strings, service characteristics, and patient communication languages can affect directory choice and access. Dropping them during down-conversion can degrade directory accuracy.

justification.inferredGoal: Improve provider directory expressiveness for networks, display labels, service characteristics, and patient communication languages.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking R4-to-R6 base alternative is needed: these are optional R6 additions that preserve R4-valid instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: `network`, `display`, `characteristic`, and `communication` improve provider-directory expressiveness without invalidating existing R4 PractitionerRole instances because all are optional additions. The compatibility issue is reverse conversion into the older R4 model, not R4-to-R6 breakage, so the added base R6 fields are justified on the available evidence.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Official R4 extensions, ConceptMaps, or cross-version mapping guidance would help preserve these values when storing R6 data in R4 systems, but those are ordinary down-conversion mitigations and should not be counted as backward-compatible R6 base alternatives. Omitting the optional R6 fields would preserve R4 shape but would fail the R6 directory-expressiveness goal.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: R6-to-R4 down-conversion can be lossy without extensions or mappings, but those are mitigation/backport strategies rather than alternative R6 base designs.

evidence.detail: R6 defines these four optional local elements.
R4 has no local PractitionerRole elements with these names or direct base equivalents.

r6NotRepresentableInR4Json.display: Dr. Example, cardiology at Downtown Clinic

examples.examplesMd: The fragment is valid only as an R6-shaped example. A base R4 PractitionerRole would need extensions or would lose these fields.

findings.narrativeMd: R6 adds several optional elements that are useful for directory display, network participation, service characteristics, and patient communication languages. They are not R4-to-R6 validation breaks, but they are important for systems that must store R6 data in R4 repositories or round-trip between versions.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old R4 instances remain valid with respect to these additions because the new elements are optional. Valid R6 instances that contain them are not valid base R4 instances. Strict R4 validators and generated R4 classes will reject the fields unless they are converted to extensions or removed.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define down-conversion policy before accepting R6 data. Prefer official or project-wide extensions for `network`, `display`, `characteristic`, and `communication` when R4 round-trip fidelity matters. If dropping these fields, document that directory semantics are lost and include tests showing the loss is expected.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: Adding optional elements is a backward-compatible R4-to-R6 design. The unavoidable compatibility issue is reverse conversion to the older R4 model. Extensions and cross-version mappings are the practical compatibility mechanism.

freshReview.narrativeMd: The listed R6 elements are optional additions: `network`, `display`, `characteristic`, and `communication`. They do not make any R4 PractitionerRole instance invalid in R6 and do not require R4 producers to change. A mixed-version system that down-converts R6 to R4 can lose these directory attributes unless it uses extensions or a profile-specific mapping, but that is a reverse-version representability issue rather than a base R4-to-R6 break. Adding first-class optional directory fields is a normal and proportionate evolution for trial-use content.
keyEvidence: R6 StructureDefinition-PractitionerRole: `network` is 0..* Reference(Organization), `display` is 0..1 string, `characteristic` is 0..* CodeableConcept, and `communication` is 0..* CodeableConcept.
R4 StructureDefinition-PractitionerRole: no same-name local elements for these four fields.
All four R6 fields are optional, so existing R4 instances remain structurally compatible in the forward direction.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 PractitionerRole is FMM 2 and trial-use. That neutral maturity context supports allowing optional model growth when it does not invalidate old instances.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: R6-to-R4 loss: valid R6 instances that populate these optional fields cannot be represented as base R4 PractitionerRole without extensions, dropping data, or custom mapping. There is no old-valid/new-invalid R4-to-R6 mechanism.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: For reverse compatibility, these concepts could have been published only as standard extensions so R4 could carry them in its extension mechanism. That would be less disruptive for down-conversion but would sacrifice first-class R6 search, code generation, documentation, and validation semantics; it is not a better base R6 design for the forward model.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: partially agree: the existing report correctly identifies no forward hard break and real R6-to-R4 loss, but I would not treat the optional additions as a medium-impact R4-to-R6 compatibility problem.

findings.title: PractitionerRole.specialty binding weakened from preferred to example

oldState.summary: R4 binds `PractitionerRole.specialty` to c80-practice-codes with preferred strength.

binding.description: Specific specialty associated with the agency.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The local compose definitions list the same SNOMED CT specialty concepts in R4 and R6, with some display text changes visible in the local files. No terminology-server expansion was run.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 encouraged use of the C80 practice-code value set for specialties.

newState.summary: R6 keeps the same value set URL but lowers the binding strength to example.

binding.description: Specific specialty associated with the agency.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: Because the binding is weaker in R6, this is not a validator hardening. The main risk is changed conformance expectations and downstream code that assumed C80 codes were preferred.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 treats the C80 practice-code set as examples rather than the preferred set for interoperability.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The path, element id, type, cardinality, value set URL, and binding description are unchanged; only binding strength and associated explanatory text changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Lowering a binding from preferred to example does not make R4 data invalid in R6. It can still affect validators, QA reports, generated enum hints, analytics, or profiles that used the R4 preferred binding as an interoperability expectation.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Specialty coding affects directory search and analytics, but the base binding weakening is not a direct safety constraint.

justification.inferredGoal: Avoid implying that the C80 practice-code set is the preferred universal specialty terminology for PractitionerRole.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: No less-breaking base alternative is needed because the binding was weakened from preferred to example and does not reject R4 instances.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Lowering the base binding strength is compatibility-friendly for R4-to-R6 instances and plausibly reflects that specialty coding varies by jurisdiction. Because the supplied evidence lacks the official change rationale, the goal is only probably justified, but the change was not accomplished with R4-to-R6 breakage.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: Keeping the R4 preferred binding would preserve stronger base guidance but would not be a less-breaking design, because the R6 example binding already preserves old data. The appropriate compatibility mechanism for systems that depend on C80 is an R6 profile or implementation guide, not an alternative base-resource shape.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: The tradeoff is weaker base interoperability guidance, not instance breakage; implementations that still need C80 practice codes can require them in profiles.

evidence.detail: R4 binding strength is preferred and valueSet is c80-practice-codes.
R6 binding strength is example with the same valueSet URL.
Local ValueSet compose content appears to retain the same listed SNOMED CT codes, with some display-text changes; no expansion was run.

examples.examplesMd: No old-valid/new-invalid example is expected because the binding weakened. An R6 instance using a non-C80 specialty code is base-valid under an example binding but might still violate local R4-era profiles or business rules.

findings.narrativeMd: The specialty binding changed from `preferred` to `example`. This is not a hard instance break, but it changes the base specification's interoperability signal. Systems that treated C80 practice codes as the expected specialty vocabulary should not assume the R6 base resource provides that same guidance.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: FHIR validators do not reject non-preferred or non-example CodeableConcepts solely because of these binding strengths. The practical effect is conformance and tooling behavior: warnings, recommendations, generated documentation, and profile inheritance may differ.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: If an implementation depends on C80 specialty coding, carry that requirement in an R6 profile or implementation guide rather than relying on the base `PractitionerRole.specialty` binding. Regression tests should distinguish base-resource validity from profile-level terminology expectations.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The change is effectively backward compatible for instances because it weakens rather than strengthens terminology expectations. A stronger binding could still be supplied by profiles where appropriate.

freshReview.narrativeMd: `PractitionerRole.specialty` keeps the same path, cardinality, datatype, and value set URL while the binding strength drops from preferred to example. That weakens base terminology pressure rather than making old data invalid. Validators, documentation generators, or enum-hint tooling may change their recommendations, but this is not a material compatibility break for instances or APIs.
keyEvidence: R4 StructureDefinition-PractitionerRole: `PractitionerRole.specialty` is 0..* `CodeableConcept` with preferred binding to `http://hl7.org/fhir/ValueSet/c80-practice-codes`.
R6 StructureDefinition-PractitionerRole: the same element remains 0..* `CodeableConcept` with the same value set URL but example binding strength.
Local R4 and R6 ValueSet-c80-practice-codes compose definitions use the same SNOMED CT value set URL and listed specialty concepts, with display-text differences visible locally.
freshReview.fmmEffect: R4 PractitionerRole is FMM 2 and trial-use. Even with a stronger maturity level this would be low concern because the computable change is a weakening, not a hardening; FMM 2 reinforces that no special stability issue is present.
freshReview.compatibilityMechanism: metadata/tooling: the binding metadata may affect recommendations, QA output, generated documentation, or profile authors' expectations. It does not create an old-valid/new-invalid instance break.
freshReview.lessBreakingAlternativeAssessment: Retaining preferred strength would preserve the old recommendation but would not be less breaking for instances; it would be more prescriptive than R6. Profiles or IGs that need stronger specialty coding expectations can still impose them.
freshReview.comparisonToExisting: agree with the existing low/no-hard-break impact assessment and with not identifying a meaningful less-breaking base alternative.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: The canonical URL, id, name, kind, type, derivation, abstract flag, and DomainResource base are unchanged. R6 maturity/status changes are noted as non-breaking metadata.

Retained local elements (`identifier`, `active`, `period`, `practitioner`, `organization`, `code`, `specialty`, `location`, `healthcareService`, and `endpoint`) keep their R4 cardinalities. Removed/replaced and added elements are covered in findings.
Retained local element type codes are unchanged. Type/domain changes for `telecom` to `contact` and old availability fields to `availability` are covered in findings.

Retained references keep the same targets: practitioner to Practitioner, organization to Organization, location to Location, healthcareService to HealthcareService, and endpoint to Endpoint. The new `network` reference to Organization is covered as an R6-only addition.

The `code` binding remains example to `practitioner-role`; `availableTime.daysOfWeek` moves into `Availability.availableTime.daysOfWeek` with a required days-of-week binding whose local compose still includes the same code system. `specialty` binding weakening is a finding. Full expansions were not run.

No local retained `PractitionerRole` constraint was tightened. The new `Availability.av-1` constraint is reported with the availability replacement. Inherited DomainResource and Element constraints are out of scope.
No local PractitionerRole element became a modifier or stopped being a modifier. Inherited modifier-extension and implicitRules details are out of scope.

Summary flags for retained local elements are unchanged. The meaningful summary-surface change from R4 `telecom` summary=true to R6 `contact` summary=false is included in the contact replacement finding.
No local fixed value, pattern, or default value constraints were found on retained PractitionerRole elements.
No local minValue, maxValue, maxLength, or regex constraints were found on retained PractitionerRole elements.
No local PractitionerRole slicing change was found. Slicing on inherited extension elements and datatype internals is outside the local resource finding set.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Artifact status and maturity advanced in R6
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 changes the artifact metadata from draft/trial-use/FMM 2 to active/normative/FMM 4, while preserving the canonical URL and resource type. This affects governance expectations, not instance wire validity.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Treat the R6 shape as more stable, but do not infer that R4 trial-use instances automatically satisfy the new R6 structural model.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 adds explanatory text about historical and non-adjacent roles
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R6 expands comments around active, period, organization, and root description semantics without changing retained cardinalities or reference targets. The new text clarifies modeling expectations rather than invalidating existing data by itself.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Review business rules that collapse multiple non-adjacent employment periods into one PractitionerRole; R6 guidance favors distinct instances for distinct non-adjacent periods.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 `PractitionerRole.availability` depends on the new reusable `Availability` datatype. Its `av-1` invariant and optional `notAvailableTime.description` materially affect migration and reverse conversion.
R6 `PractitionerRole.contact` depends on `ExtendedContactDetail`, whose richer fields drive the main R6-to-R4 representability risk for contact information.

Inherited base-resource changes, including Resource.language binding and DomainResource contained-resource invariant text/expression changes, are excluded from this local PractitionerRole report and should be owned by base-artifact reports.

Element replacement from `telecom` to `contact` and availability restructuring may have corresponding search parameter changes; search parameters are out of scope for this resource StructureDefinition report.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The assessment is based on local package artifacts, not an official HL7 R4-to-R6 diff, Jira issue trail, or ballot reconciliation notes. Justification assessments are therefore inferred from the structural changes.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: An official change log or Jira proposals for PractitionerRole contact and availability redesigns would improve rationale confidence.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology comparison used local ValueSet compose content only. No terminology server expansion was run for SNOMED CT, all-languages, service-mode, or contactentity-type, so code-level additions/removals are not fully assessed.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run expansions against the intended terminology server and SNOMED CT edition/version, then compare code sets and display/status changes.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: `Availability` and `ExtendedContactDetail` were inspected only to explain their local use by PractitionerRole. This report does not replace a full breaking-change assessment of those datatypes or their inherited datatype/base changes.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Complete separate datatype reports for `Availability` and `ExtendedContactDetail`.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The R6 input is a ballot build (`6.0.0-ballot4`), not a final published release. Element names, comments, or bindings could change before final R6 publication.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Re-run the assessment against the final R6 package when available.
